This bill moves responsibility for four family engagement programs for elementary and secondary schools from the Department of Education to the Department of Health and Human Services. The programs are Family Engagement in Education Programs, Community Support for School Success, National Activities for School Safety, and Ready to Learn Programming. The bill also moves the staff and funding tied to those functions to the new department.

The bill says the Office of Management and Budget oversees this transfer. That office must make sure the change does not increase the number of full-time equivalent employees at either department. It must also certify to specified congressional committees that the bill is being followed.

The bill notes that in February 2026, the Department of Education announced an agreement with the Department of Health and Human Services for that department to provide services supporting these programs.

Finally, the transfer does not affect any lawsuits, proceedings, or applications for benefits, services, licenses, permits, certificates, or financial assistance that are already pending when the bill becomes law.

summary.text:
Less Bureaucracy, Better Family Engagement Act
This bill transfers specified functions relating to family engagement programs for elementary and secondary education from the Department of Education (ED) to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS).
Specifically, the bill transfers to HHS all the functions and authorities exercised by ED before the bill's effective date related to the following four programs: Family Engagement in Education Programs, the Community Support for School Success program, the National Activities for School Safety program, and the Ready to Learn Programming program. (In February 2026, ED announced an interagency agreement with HHS for HHS to provide services supporting the administration of these programs.)
Additionally, the bill transfers to HHS all personnel and appropriations related to the functions that are transferred under this bill.
The bill outlines the authority of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) related to the functions that are transferred under this bill, including that OMB must ensure that this bill does not create a net increase in full-time equivalent employees at HHS or ED. Further, OMB must certify compliance with the bill to specified congressional committees.
The transfer of these functions does not affect any suits, proceedings, or applications for benefits, services, licenses, permits, certificates, or financial assistance that are pending on the date of this bill's enactment.
